Class VanillaSlotResolver

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.api.slot.VanillaSlotResolver
public final class VanillaSlotResolver extends Object
Finds where a player-inventory slot is on whatever screen is open. You name player-inventory slot N and get back its rectangle; MenuKit handles the slot loop and creative's SlotWrapper, so you write no per-screen geometry.

Panel anchoring (SlotGroupCategories, SlotGroupPanelAdapter) places panels against a category of slots by slicing menu.slots. This answers a different question: where on this screen is the one slot whose player-inventory index is N? It matches by identity (container and getContainerSlot), which creative's SlotWrapper hides, so it goes through Slots.target(Slot): identity from the unwrapped slot, position from the in-menu slot (the wrapper, which has the creative coordinates).

containerIndex is the slot's index in the player Inventory, the value Slot.getContainerSlot() reports for a raw player slot: 0 to 8 for the hotbar, 9 to 35 for the main inventory, and the player's equipment indices for armour and offhand. Any player-inventory slot works, not just the hotbar.

It works on any screen whose menu shows the player inventory: the survival inventory, the creative inventory tab (wrapped slots), and container screens such as chests and furnaces, which build their own player-inventory slots. No per-menu resolver is needed, because the slots themselves know they belong to the player Inventory.

Client only: it reads the screen frame and the creative wrapper.
